clue.text: Time limits second fatal quality

parts.note: deadlines are limits of time for finishing a task

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a second's overrun on time limits can prove fatal.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun from deadly: the property of being able to kill, a fatal nature.

clue.text: Stupid duke gets back

parts.note: D is an abbreviation for duke in titles
aft means at the back, especially of a ship

explanation.surface: A dim aristocrat is getting his comeuppance.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone foolish or silly.

clue.text: A fool turned up around final item for discussion

indicators.note: around says the reversed fool wraps the word for final
in a down clue, turned up means the word for fool is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A clown pops up near the last point on a meeting's list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' gives GUM, read upwards in this down clue; 'final' is wordplay, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Agendum is the singular of agenda: a single matter on a meeting's list to be talked over.

clue.text: He helps keep sailors safe although mines exploded

indicators.note: something exploded is blown apart, so the letters of the fodder are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Praise for a man who protects seafarers even though the waters around are mined.
explanation.definitionFit: A keeper of a coastal beacon tower whose light warns ships off rocks.

clue.text: Unspoilt countryside turning brown over river

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: Fields are going brown beside a river in a rural scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Nature is the natural world, untouched by people, as in countryside left wild.

clue.text: Given spice — caraway perhaps — a boy is tucking in

indicators.note: tucking in describes the seed taking the other pieces inside it

parts.note: caraway is an example of a seed used as a spice
a son is a boy child

explanation.surface: A lad tucks into food flavoured with caraway.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasoned food has had flavourings such as herbs and spices added.

clue.text: Rugby player's item used in play

definitions.meaning: a forward in the front row of the scrum
a property, an object handled by actors on stage

explanation.surface: A rugby player's kit used during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a front-row forward in rugby, and a theatrical property short for property.

clue.text: Go wild seeing smallest item of litter dropped round Brazilian city

Rio de Janeiro, usually just Rio

explanation.walkthrough: 'litter' looks like rubbish but means a brood of young animals.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to behave in an unrestrained, uncontrolled way.

clue.text: Friend at airstrip needed radar perhaps

parts.note: a pal is a friend
at and in both mean present at a place
a drome is short for aerodrome, an airfield

explanation.surface: A mate at the airfield needs radar equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar is an example of a word that reads the same backwards and forwards.

clue.text: Worry about American soldier returning hot goods

explanation.surface: Concern about a US serviceman coming back with stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot' looks like stolen, but is just the tap abbreviation. 'returning' turns the soldier round, and 'about' wraps the worry round that and the H.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight is cargo, the goods carried by a ship, train or lorry.

clue.text: Football club magazine

definitions.meaning: the north London Premier League club
a store of arms and ammunition

explanation.surface: A club's own matchday magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a London football club, and a store of weapons, as a magazine also is.

clue.text: Childish game about Emma Peel, say, in crash

explanation.definitionFit: A party game in which children hunt for a list of items to collect.

clue.text: Decline to check current address

parts.note: to deter is to check or discourage

an oration is a formal speech or address

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to inspect the present address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' reads as a verb, refusing, but defines a noun for a worsening.
explanation.definitionFit: A decline is a worsening of condition over time.

clue.text: Booty left for antisocial type

parts.note: spoils are plunder or loot
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Plunder abandoned by someone unsociable.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who ruins others' fun, an unsociable killjoy.

clue.text: Ceremony accompanying one decoration or another

definitions.note: short for another decoration, a noun

parts.note: pomp is splendid ceremonial display
the OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A ceremony at which honours of one kind or another are handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' carries over 'decoration' from before it: a second kind of decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: A woolly bobble used as ornament on hats is a decoration of a different sort.

clue.text: Sapper, favourite after loading a Queen's gun

indicators.note: after places the favourite piece behind the sapper

parts.note: a pet is a favourite
ER, Elizabeth Regina

clue.text: Hook may set out to reach a Japanese port

indicators.note: set out means the letters are laid out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: Captain Hook may sail off to reach a port in Japan.

clue.text: I am after gold fake

parts.note: contracted to I'm
post is Latin for after
or is gold in heraldry

clue.text: Looks to hoard the French old coppers

clue.text: Shining silver light almost encircling earth

explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts LAMP to LAM, and 'encircling' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Agleam means glinting, giving off a gleam of light.

clue.text: One in Sweden confused, back to front

indicators.note: confused means the letters are muddled into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' only links I to SWEDEN; 'confused' rearranges all seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Endwise means with the end forward, so turned the other way round.

clue.text: International target investing pounds, billions, separately

separately means the two letters go in at different points, not side by side

clue.text: Solderer worked with metal forced through

clue.text: A canoe I manoeuvred round group of Pacific islands

explanation.definitionFit: The name for the islands of the central and south Pacific, often including Australasia.

clue.text: Uncivilised church leader out of work accepts boring routine

clue.text: Pilot's ordeal

definitions.meaning: a trial run, as in a pilot study

explanation.surface: A flier's terrible experience.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a trial run like a pilot scheme, and a hard trial of endurance.

clue.text: Financial district cash-holder must accept rest being disturbed

indicators.note: being disturbed means the letters of rest are jumbled
